html:
Pachacuti was the ninth Sapa Inca, the ruler who turned the small kingdom of Cusco into the Inca Empire in the mid 1400s. His dates are uncertain; his reign is usually given as 1438 to 1471.

Inca tradition says he came to power in a crisis. The Chanka people attacked Cusco, his father and the heir fled, and the young prince stayed to defend the city and won. He then took the throne and the name Pachacuti, meaning "turn of the world" or "earth shaker".

What he did, by the Inca accounts:

  • Conquest: he took lands around Lake Titicaca and far north and south, beginning the expansion that his son Topa Inca Yupanqui and grandson Huayna Capac carried to Ecuador and Chile.
  • Cusco: he rebuilt the capital in fine fitted stone, with the Coricancha, the temple of the sun, at its heart.
  • Religion: he raised the cult of Inti, the sun god, and is said to have set up the Inti Raymi festival.
  • Estates: Machu Picchu was most likely built as one of his royal estates.

He also shaped the system of rule: roads, storehouses, labour service and the record keeping of the quipu. After his death his mummy was kept in Cusco and cared for as if he still lived, with his lineage keeping his estates. Spanish chroniclers wrote down his story from these Inca memories, which is why it mixes history and legend.
sum: Pachacuti was the ninth Sapa Inca, the ruler who turned the small kingdom of Cusco into the Inca Empire in the mid 1400s. His dates are uncertain; his reign is usually given as 1438 to 1471.
